newsitem.title: JAPAN: New entity to take over PNC fast-breeder programme.
newsitem.headline: New entity to take over PNC fast-breeder programme.

text.p: A government advisory panel said on Monday that Japan's fast-breeder reactor development programme would be among the functions to be taken over by a new entity which will replace the nation's troubled state-run nuclear power firm.
This, together with a research and development programme for radioactive waste management, should form the nucleus of the new entity, the panel said in a draft report.

The panel has been meeting since April to discuss how to restructure the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), whose credibility has deteriorated after a series of accidents at its nuclear power facilities.
A prototype fast-breeder nuclear reactor operated by PNC has been shut since a sodium coolant leakage accident in 1995.
A fire and explosion at PNC's Tokai nuclear fuel reprocessing plant exposed 37 workers to low levels of radiation in March this year. The plant remains shut.
About a month after the accident, PNC was ordered to halt operations of its Fugen prototype nuclear reactor after it failed to immediately report a radiation leak at the plant.
The advisory panel plans to release its final report on how PNC should be restructured and a specific timetable at its next and last meeting, scheduled for July 30.
Monday's report said the Tokai reprocessing plant, in Ibaragi prefecture northeast of Tokyo, should continue operations.
It said, however, that Fugen should eventually stop operations and should then be used for research on scrapping nuclear reactors.
PNC's programme to explore for and refine uranium will either be transferred to the private sector or be gradually scrapped, the draft said.
